subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechco.com>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.example>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through the product and the performance overview. I promised to follow up with a concise recap and a proposed SLO checklist so we can align on decision criteria and next steps. Attached are: 1) the SLO checklist (spreadsheet) and 2) the post-demo slides with the perf numbers we showed.

High-level items from our conversation (please confirm or correct):
- Primary workload: real-time customer chat (streaming responses) powering in-product support flows.
- Target concurrency: ~10 active sessions per second for critical path; burst up to 25.
- Steady throughput target: 120 concurrent requests/sec (avg) across the service during peak business hours.
- Latency targets (customer requirement): p95 end-to-end (request->first-token stream start) <= 200 ms; p99 <= 350 ms.
- Token lengths: typical session ~100 tokens response; worst-case ~800 tokens for long-form summaries.
- Streaming required (token-by-token partials) with low time-to-first-token.
- Acceptable fallback behavior: graceful degrade to smaller model variant (maintain availability) if latency SLO violated.

Proposed next steps / MAP items (owners in parens):
1) Confirm SLO targets and traffic profile (Samir / Elena) — reply with any adjustments by EOD Tue.
2) Provide representative sample traffic (anonymized) and 1-2 long sessions for perf testing (Elena) — ETA 4/15.
3) Redwood run: scoped perf run (non-prod) to validate p95/p99 and throughput with streaming enabled (Aditya) — target week of 4/20.
4) Initial capacity recommendation and cost estimate (Priyom) — deliverable by 4/22.
5) Security/compliance checklist & procurement kickoff (Marissa) — I'll start the procurement thread after perf validation.

Questions for you now:
- Are the latency numbers above (p95 <= 200ms / p99 <= 350ms) aligned with what the product team needs?
- Can you share a small anonymized trace (1-3 sessions) that includes the longest expected response (800 tokens)?

Attachments: fintechco-slo-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 12KB); post-demo-performance-slides.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

Thanks — look forward to locking the MAP.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.example

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 17:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks Marissa — very helpful summary. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Latency: p95 <= 200ms is what the PM is asking for on the chat surface; p99 requirement is softer — we can accept up to 400 ms at p99 for long sessions, but would prefer <= 350 ms if feasible.
- Throughput/concurrency: our internal telemetry shows average peak ~90 RPS but with spiky bursts to ~200 RPS during product launches. The concurrency number we mentioned (10 active sessions/sec) maps to ~120 RPS for our typical message sizes; the burst profile is the main concern.
- Streaming: required for real-time UX (must see first tokens within 150-200 ms).

We can share anonymized traces — Elena will attach 2 sessions (one short, one long) by 4/15. For the perf run, please include a burst test that ramps to 200 RPS for 2 minutes and sustained runs at 120 RPS for 10 minutes. Also include a test that simulates 800-token responses to capture tail behavior.

On procurement: once we validate perf numbers we'll be ready to get pricing and a short-term trial.

Samir
Samir Shah
Director, Product — FintechCo
samir.shah@fintechco.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.example>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.example>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 07:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Appreciate the clear targets, Samir. A few technical notes and proposal for the perf run:

- Time-to-first-token: our streaming path prioritizes first-token latency; we expect to be able to meet the 150-200 ms TTF target for the short (~100-token) responses on a properly sized pool. Long responses (800 tokens) are more about overall throughput and memory/KV cache behavior — first-token still should be quick but tail tokens will be linear in generation time.
- Burst handling: we'll include a test that ramps to 200 RPS for 2 minutes with concurrent model warm-up. Expect some queuing; we can tune batching windows and autoscale policy to reduce queuing for short requests.
- Suggested initial test config:
  * Model variant: redwood/llama-2-chat-16k (or a smaller low-latency variant if you prefer)
  * Pool: Dedicated trial with 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (we'll provide an estimate)
  * Batching: adaptive batching with max latency budget 60ms for short tokens
  * KV/prefix caching: enable for repeated prompts (we'll need the sample traffic to configure keys)

Action items from engineering (owners):
- Aditya: run the scoped perf run (non-prod) and produce a perf report with p50/p95/p99, memory, and GPU utilization. Target window: week of 4/20.
- Priyom: capacity + cost estimate based on perf run.
- Soojin: prepare a streaming test harness and make sure SDK hooks are included for time-to-first-token measurement.

One question: do you have any regulatory or data residency constraints we should consider for the perf environment (e.g., must run in us-east-1)?

—Aditya
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.example

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintechco.com>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.example>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.example>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks — this is perfect. Quick summary / next steps and owners so everyone has the MAP:

1) FintechCo to confirm final latency & burst acceptance (Samir) — confirmation by Tue 4/14.
2) FintechCo to share anonymized traces (Elena) — files due 4/15.
3) Redwood perf run (Aditya) — week of 4/20. Deliverable: perf report + log export.
4) Capacity & cost estimate (Priyom) — deliverable by 4/22.
5) Streaming test harness (Soojin) — include TTF metrics + SDK hooks; ready by perf run start.
6) Procurement kickoff (Marissa) — I'll open procurement thread after perf report looks good.

Decision criteria for go/no-go after perf run:
- Meet p95 <= 200ms for short responses and TTF <= 200ms for streaming.
- Sustained throughput of 120 RPS with ability to absorb 2-minute bursts to 200 RPS without violating p95 by more than 20%.
- Reasonable cost envelope (Priyom will propose options for reserved vs trial Dedicated).

I'll track these as a simple MAP and post updates in the shared Drive folder. If nothing else, please reply here to confirm the timeline.

Best —
Marissa
